text: In 2018, King Mswati III officially changed the name of his country from $\textbf{Swaziland}$ to $\textbf{Eswatini}$ to mark the 50th anniversary of independence.
explanation: The name means 'land of the Swazis' in the Swazi language and was changed partly to avoid confusion with Switzerland.

text: The $\textbf{Kilauea}$ volcano in $\textbf{Hawaii}$ experienced a massive lower Puna eruption in 2018, destroying hundreds of homes and reshaping the coastline.
explanation: It was one of the most destructive eruptions in Hawaii's modern history, adding hundreds of acres of new land to the Big Island.

text: The $\textbf{Tham Luang}$ cave complex, where a junior football team was trapped and successfully rescued in 2018, is located in the Chiang Rai province of $\textbf{Thailand}$.
explanation: The dramatic rescue operation involved international divers and highlighted the treacherous geography of the flooded cave system.

text: The $\textbf{Camp Fire}$, the deadliest and most destructive wildfire in $\textbf{California}$ history, virtually destroyed the town of $\textbf{Paradise}$ in 2018.
explanation: The fire was ignited by faulty electrical transmission lines and spread rapidly due to extreme drought conditions.

text: The $\textbf{Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge}$, the world's longest sea-crossing bridge, opened in 2018, connecting cities across the $\textbf{Pearl River Delta}$.
explanation: This massive infrastructure project links Hong Kong, Macau, and mainland China physically.

text: A devastating earthquake and tsunami struck the island of $\textbf{Sulawesi}$ in $\textbf{Indonesia}$ in 2018, severely damaging the city of $\textbf{Palu}$.
explanation: The unique geography of Palu bay amplified the tsunami waves, causing widespread destruction.

text: The $\textbf{Volcán de Fuego}$ erupted violently in June 2018, causing deadly pyroclastic flows in $\textbf{Guatemala}$.
explanation: It is one of Central America's most active volcanoes, located near the colonial city of Antigua.

text: In 2018, the city of $\textbf{Cape Town}$ in $\textbf{South Africa}$ narrowly avoided 'Day Zero', the day when municipal water taps would be turned off due to severe $\textbf{Drought}$.
explanation: Severe water restrictions and public cooperation helped the city avert the crisis.

text: The $\textbf{Anak Krakatau}$ volcano in the $\textbf{Sunda Strait}$ collapsed in late 2018, triggering a deadly tsunami that hit the coasts of Java and Sumatra.
explanation: Anak Krakatau ('Child of Krakatoa') emerged from the caldera of the famous 1883 eruption.

text: The 2018 $\textbf{Winter Olympics}$ were held in $\textbf{PyeongChang}$, a county in the Taebaek Mountains of $\textbf{South Korea}$.
explanation: The games were notable for the joint march of North and South Korean athletes under a unified flag.

text: Hurricane $\textbf{Michael}$ made landfall in the $\textbf{Florida Panhandle}$ in 2018 as a Category 5 storm, destroying the Tyndall Air Force Base.
explanation: It was the first Category 5 hurricane to strike the contiguous United States since Hurricane Andrew in 1992.

text: The $\textbf{Yellow Vest}$ protests (Gilets Jaunes) began in 2018 across $\textbf{France}$, initially sparked by rising fuel prices and the cost of living.
explanation: The movement paralyzed major transport routes and landmarks like the Champs-Élysées.

text: The $\textbf{Prespa Agreement}$, signed in 2018, resolved the long-standing name dispute between $\textbf{Greece}$ and the country now known as $\textbf{North Macedonia}$.
explanation: The dispute arose because Greece has a northern region also named Macedonia.

text: The $\textbf{Morandi Bridge}$ collapsed in the Italian city of $\textbf{Genoa}$ in 2018, severing a vital transport link to France.
explanation: The disaster highlighted the aging infrastructure issues facing many European nations.

text: The $\textbf{2018 FIFA World Cup}$ was hosted by $\textbf{Russia}$, spanning two continents (Europe and Asia) across 11 cities.
explanation: It was the first World Cup to be held in Eastern Europe.

text: The $\textbf{Kerala}$ floods in 2018 were the worst floods in nearly a century to hit this southwestern state of $\textbf{India}$.
explanation: Unusually high rainfall during the monsoon season caused dams to open, inundating the region.

text: In 2018, $\textbf{Eritrea}$ and $\textbf{Ethiopia}$ signed a peace deal ending decades of 'frozen conflict' in the $\textbf{Horn of Africa}$.
explanation: The border was reopened for the first time in 20 years, reuniting families.

text: The $\textbf{Bering Sea}$ experienced unprecedented low levels of winter $\textbf{Sea Ice}$ in 2018, alarming climate scientists.
explanation: This anomaly disrupted indigenous hunting practices and marine ecosystems.

text: The $\textbf{Sentinelese}$ people, an uncontacted tribe living on $\textbf{North Sentinel Island}$ in the Bay of Bengal, made headlines in 2018 following an intrusion incident.
explanation: The island is part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands territory of India and is strictly off-limits.

text: The $\textbf{G20 Summit}$ in 2018 was held in $\textbf{Buenos Aires}$, the capital of $\textbf{Argentina}$, marking the first G20 summit in South America.
explanation: Leaders discussed trade, climate change, and sustainable development.

text: The $\textbf{United States}$ officially moved its embassy in $\textbf{Israel}$ from Tel Aviv to $\textbf{Jerusalem}$ in May 2018.
explanation: The move was controversial because Jerusalem's status is a central issue in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

text: The $\textbf{Lake Turkana}$ National Parks in $\textbf{Kenya}$ were placed on the List of World Heritage in Danger in 2018 due to dam construction.
explanation: The Gibe III dam in Ethiopia threatened the water levels of the lake, which is the world's largest desert lake.

text: Typhoon $\textbf{Mangkhut}$ was the strongest storm of 2018, causing widespread destruction in the $\textbf{Philippines}$ and $\textbf{South China}$ in September.
explanation: It made landfall on the island of Luzon before hitting Hong Kong and mainland China.

text: A referendum on independence from $\textbf{France}$ was held in $\textbf{New Caledonia}$ in 2018, with the majority voting to remain part of France.
explanation: New Caledonia is a special collectivity of France located in the southwest Pacific Ocean.

text: The $\textbf{Sanchi}$ oil tanker collision occurred in the $\textbf{East China Sea}$, resulting in the world's largest condensate oil spill in decades.
explanation: The tanker burned for over a week before sinking, releasing toxic light oil.

text: The $\textbf{Panmunjom Declaration}$ was signed in 2018 by leaders of North and South Korea at the $\textbf{Demilitarized Zone (DMZ)}$.
explanation: The summit aimed to formally end the Korean War and denuclearize the peninsula.

text: In 2018, researchers published evidence that the $\textbf{Great Pacific Garbage Patch}$ is much larger than previously thought, located between $\textbf{California}$ and $\textbf{Hawaii}$.
explanation: The patch consists of millions of tons of floating plastic debris.

text: The $\textbf{Lion Air}$ Flight 610 crash occurred in the $\textbf{Java Sea}$ shortly after taking off from Jakarta, $\textbf{Indonesia}$.
explanation: This was the first of two fatal crashes involving the Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft.

text: The $\textbf{IPCC Special Report}$ on Global Warming of $\textbf{1.5°C}$ was released in 2018 in Incheon, $\textbf{South Korea}$, outlining the impacts of global heating.
explanation: The report emphasized the urgent need to limit warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.

text: The $\textbf{Hokkaido Eastern Iburi earthquake}$ struck the northernmost main island of $\textbf{Japan}$ in 2018, causing massive landslides.
explanation: Hokkaido is known for its volcanoes, natural hot springs (onsen), and ski areas.

text: The $\textbf{Mount Etna}$, Europe's highest active volcano located in $\textbf{Sicily}$, Italy, erupted late in 2018 causing earthquakes.
explanation: Etna is one of the world's most active volcanoes and is in an almost constant state of activity.

text: The $\textbf{Louvre Abu Dhabi}$, which saw its first full year of operations in 2018, is a major cultural museum located in the $\textbf{United Arab Emirates}$.
explanation: It is located on Saadiyat Island and is part of a cultural district in the capital.

text: The $\textbf{Qantas}$ airline launched the first non-stop commercial flight from $\textbf{Perth}$ to $\textbf{London}$ in 2018, covering 14,498 km.
explanation: This 'Kangaroo Route' flight takes approximately 17 hours, connecting Australia directly to Europe.

text: The $\textbf{Lake Chad}$ region was the focus of a high-level conference in 2018 to address its shrinking water levels and the humanitarian crisis in the $\textbf{Sahel}$.
explanation: The lake has shrunk by 90% since the 1960s, affecting Chad, Nigeria, Niger, and Cameroon.

text: The $\textbf{Mount Agung}$ volcano in $\textbf{Bali}$, Indonesia, erupted in mid-2018, disrupting flights and tourism on the popular island.
explanation: Bali is a major tourist destination known for its volcanic mountains, beaches, and coral reefs.

text: The $\textbf{Rohingya}$ refugee crisis continued in 2018, with vast camps located in $\textbf{Cox's Bazar}$, Bangladesh, near the border with $\textbf{Myanmar}$.
explanation: Cox's Bazar became home to the world's largest refugee camp.

text: The $\textbf{Trans-Alaska Pipeline}$ was shut down briefly in 2018 following a 7.0 magnitude earthquake near $\textbf{Anchorage}$.
explanation: The pipeline transports oil from the North Slope to Valdez.

text: The $\textbf{Lombok}$ earthquake in 2018 caused significant damage to the island, which sits just east of $\textbf{Bali}$ in Indonesia.
explanation: The Wallace Line, a faunal boundary line, runs between Bali and Lombok.

text: The $\textbf{Vistula Spit}$ canal project was initiated by $\textbf{Poland}$ in 2018 to allow ships to bypass Russian waters near Kaliningrad.
explanation: The canal connects the Vistula Lagoon with the Gdańsk Bay.

text: The $\textbf{Montecito}$ mudslides in early 2018 occurred in Southern $\textbf{California}$, triggered by heavy rain on land burnt by the $\textbf{Thomas Fire}$.
explanation: This disaster highlighted the dangerous 'fire-flood' cycle often seen in the region's geography.
